title: After Nadir Leaves, Zakariya Khan Turns Again on the Singhs

blocks.text: The page first closes the Nadir Shah episode with a reflective note: some persecutors died in the turmoil, while others survived only long enough to continue unfinished violence. The poet presents this as received tradition, heard from elders who remembered both judgment and survival.

It then pivots decisively after Nadir left for Kabul. Humiliated rather than corrected, Khan Bahadur and Zakariya Khan return their rage toward the Sikhs and prepare a renewed campaign to scour the land of keshdhari Singhs.

That transition matters because it marks a change from imperial collapse to local repression. Foreign invasion passes, but the machinery of anti-Sikh persecution remains in place and begins operating with even more bitterness than before.
